timeline.tag: Chronicles of Sweetness • 8,000 BC to Present
timeline.title: The Ancient Odyssey Of Cane
timeline.sub: Trace how a wild Pacific grass became the world's most cherished botanical elixir across six millennia of human civilization.

milestones.title: Domestication of Saccharum
milestones.desc: Indigenous farmers in Papua New Guinea first cultivate wild Saccharum robustum, chewing raw stalks for pure natural sustenance.

milestones.title: First Crystal Sugar & Ayurveda
milestones.desc: Indian scholars discover how to crystallize cane juice into 'Khanda' (the origin of the word candy) and document its cooling digestive benefits in Ayurvedic texts.

milestones.title: The Golden Age of Cane Mills
milestones.desc: Persian and Arab agronomists engineer sophisticated water-powered crushing mills, introducing cold sugarcane extraction to Egypt, Sicily, and Spain.

milestones.title: Global Maritime Expansion
milestones.desc: Sugarcane seedlings cross the Atlantic, flourishing in fertile volcanic soils and becoming the cornerstone of international botanical trade.

milestones.title: The Cane House Renaissance
milestones.desc: We revive the forgotten art of raw, cold-pressed sugarcane juice — unadulterated, unpasteurized, and freshly poured for London's communities.

history.title: History Of Sugarcane
history.sub: Originating in New Guinea, sugarcane spread across Asia, the Middle East, Europe and the world. It played a vital role in trade, economies and cultures for centuries.

life_cycle.title: Life Cycle Of Sugarcane
life_cycle.sub: From fertile volcanic soils to the final fresh-pressed London pour — explore every biological stage of the ancient Saccharum officinarum plant.

items.label: Sett Planting & Sprouting
items.fact: Selected 2-3 eye cuttings in fertile furrows
items.desc: Prime mature cane cuttings (setts) are planted horizontally in deep, nutrient-rich compost beds, sprouting tender roots and vigorous green shoots.

items.label: Tillering & Canopy Growth
items.fact: 6 to 8 healthy secondary shoots per plant
items.desc: Under abundant rainfall and tropical sunlight, dense emerald foliage unfurls, creating a natural soil-shading canopy that conserves moisture.

items.label: Grand Growth & Jointing
items.fact: Reaches 3 to 5 metres with thick sucrose nodes
items.desc: The fibrous stalks surge upward, developing segmented bamboo-like nodes that synthesize and store pure sweet sucrose through natural photosynthesis.

items.label: Ripening & Sucrose Peak
items.desc: As vegetative growth subsides in the cooler season, the stalks concentrate natural complex sugars, iron, magnesium, potassium, and active antioxidants.

items.label: Sustainable Hand Harvest
items.fact: Hand-cut at soil level to preserve root ratoon
items.desc: Skilled farmers hand-harvest only prime stalks at soil level, allowing the living ratoon root system to regrow organically for the next cycle.

items.label: Cold-Press & Micro-Filtration
items.fact: Chilled single-pass heavy stainless steel press
items.desc: Stalks are washed in pure filtered water and cold-pressed through heavy calibrated rollers, extracting vibrant green raw juice with zero heat friction.

items.label: Pure London Pour
items.desc: Poured straight over ice with crushed organic ginger and zesty lemon for an unadulterated, mineral-rich superfood beverage.

varieties.title: Heirloom Cane Varieties
varieties.sub: Different soils and climates produce distinct cane cultivars, each with unique mineral profiles, sweetness indices, and pressing characteristics.

items.name: Noble Cane
items.profile: Crisp honey-caramel with floral undertones and high natural juice volume.

items.name: Ribbon Stripe Cane
items.profile: Aromatic grassy sweetness with rich herbaceous complexity and refreshing acidity.

items.name: Wild Purple Cane
items.profile: Deep earthy richness packed with natural anthocyanins, polyphenols, and iron.

items.name: Golden Bamboo Cane
items.profile: Silky smooth, low-fiber tender stalks that yield a vibrant lime-tinted nectar.

nutritional_alchemy.sub: Unlike refined white sugar which is chemically stripped of all nutrients, 100% raw cold-pressed cane juice is an unrefined whole-plant tonic rich in vital electrolytes.

minerals.name: Calcium

minerals.name: Bio-Iron

minerals.name: Zinc

minerals.name: Low Glycemic

storage_guide.title: How To Store & Enjoy
storage_guide.sub: Cold-pressed raw sugarcane juice contains live botanical enzymes. Follow our artisanal handling rules for peak flavour.

tips.title: Keep Strictly Chilled
tips.desc: Store between 2°C and 5°C. Raw cane contains zero thermal pasteurization, so chill immediately.

tips.title: Gentle Shake Before Pour
tips.desc: Natural micro-plant fiber and mineral salts settle at the bottom. A gentle swirl reunites the full body.

tips.title: Enjoy Within 48 Hours
tips.desc: Best consumed within 24–48 hours of pressing for peak enzymatic vibrancy and crisp botanical aroma.

tips.title: Pair With Citrus & Spice
tips.desc: Enhance with a squeeze of fresh lime, crushed ginger, or a sprig of garden mint for an authentic London pour.

items.question: Is sugarcane juice safe for diabetics?
items.answer: In moderation, and best discussed with your doctor - it is naturally sweet with no added sugar, but still a source of natural sugars.

items.question: Does sugarcane juice have calories?
items.answer: Yes, naturally - it's a whole-plant drink, not a diet product, but it has none of the artificial additives found in most soft drinks.

items.question: How is your juice different?
items.answer: Pressed fresh in front of you, from cane sourced the same day - never bottled, never stored.

items.question: Is your juice 100% natural?
items.answer: Yes - no added sugar, colours, or preservatives, ever.

items.question: How should I store it?
items.answer: It's best enjoyed fresh, right after pressing - like any fresh juice, it doesn't keep well overnight.

closing.sub: Sugarcane is more than a crop. It is a legacy. A gift from nature. A symbol of life. At The Cane House, we honour this timeless sweetness, and bring it to you - fresh, pure, and full of goodness.
